metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe-index purls <data-dir> <purl> --json`: the describes-index lookup — packages whose `describes` (whole-package or subskill) matches a PURL, plus the unusable versions that WOULD have matched it. Read by scripts and agents (PROP-044 §6.5 — a CLI `--json` report is a format plain text; `foreign_parsers = many`). Source of truth for the writer: `crates/vibe-index/src/cli/purls.rs` (`Envelope`, `Row`); the generated reader this schema owns lives in `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index_cli/e1/purls_report/`.
The package URL the ask named, echoed back verbatim.
How many rows `hits` carries. `usize` in the writer; JTD (RFC 8927) stops at 32-bit integers, so `uint32` is the narrowest true claim this language can make.
Every usable version describing the PURL, in the lookup's deterministic order. Required member: a PURL nothing describes writes `[]`, never an absent key — the writer has no skip here.
Unusable versions that WOULD have matched the requested PURL — named, not hidden (PROP-044 §4.5). Absent when there are none (the writer carries `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`).
One version describing the requested PURL.
The version's kind — metadata per PROP-008 §2.3.
Where the `describes` binding was declared: the package as a whole, or one of its subskills.

Which half of a package declared the `describes` binding (closed vocabulary of two): `package` — the version's own `describes` field matched the ask verbatim; `subskill` — a subskill's `describes` did (the version carries the binding transitively). Closed because both values name a place in the writer's own model — a third value would name a place that does not exist.

One version this build refused to act on, and why — the row every `vibe-index` answering surface carries (`crates/vibe-index/src/index/quarantine.rs`, `Unavailable`). Local to this schema family: `formats/vocabularies.json` does not (yet) carry it, and each of the six report schemas that need it declare their own copy.
The refused version's bare package name.

The reader capabilities of `must_understand` this build lacks, in the record's own order. Required member: a refusal always writes its list, `[]` never occurring in practice today (a row exists exactly because the list is non-empty) but lawful on the wire — the writer has no skip here.
What a person or a script does about it — the fixed two-part text `recipe_for` builds (the explanation with the PROP-044 anchor, then the `fix:` surface).
